chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillah, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, said:
I heard Muʿammar ibn Abi Riʾab asking Aba ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, while I was present, about the qunut in Jumuʿah, so he said: “There is no qunut in it.”
So the proper approach regarding these two reports is that we carry them upon the circumstance of taqiyyah, and that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under particular circumstances
key_terms.الْخَبَرَيْنِ: the two reports being compared or reconciled
key_terms.الْقُنُوتِ: the supplicatory invocation recited in salat at a designated point
key_terms.الْوَجْهُ: the interpretive approach or manner of reconciling the reports
key_terms.لَيْسَ: an expression of negation indicating absence of the practice here

ai.seo_question: Is there qunut in Salat al-Jumuʿah according to hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of qunut in Salat al-Jumuʿah and transmits a statement from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام that there is no qunut in it. The concluding line frames the reconciliation of reports by placing this narration in the context of taqiyyah, reflecting a juristic method in hadith analysis.
